pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome – Ethos & Values – William Davies Primary School
pageCache.text:
A Letter from the Headteacher
William Davies is a special place, developing resilient learners who are confident and adaptable. Our curriculum has been designed to give every child an experience and language rich education within our ethos of ensuring everyone at William Davies is Safe, Happy, Challenged and Makes Memories. We do this by pursuing our belief that children should be empowered to become powerful learners by instilling our Learning Powers: Be Curious, Be Resilient, Be Enthusiastic, Be Collaborative, Be Reflective, Be Adventurous.
We believe in creating a school community where every child feels valued, safe, and motivated to learn. Our school is a welcoming, caring place where relationships between staff, children and families are at the heart of everything we do. We are delighted that our children enjoy coming to school and are eager to engage in their learning. They are focused, well-behaved, and take pride in their school, as they work together with staff to create a positive atmosphere. Visitors to our school often comment on the supportive, caring ‘family’ atmosphere and respectful warm interactions between all members of our community.
We have high expectations for all and we are proud of their achievements, both academically and in their personal development. Our dedicated staff work hard to ensure that every pupil receives the support they need to succeed, from a carefully planned and ambitious curriculum to extra help for those who need it. We also prioritise the development of our pupils’ wider skills, such as communication, teamwork, and leadership, with many opportunities for children to take on responsibilities.
We know that education is about more than just academic success—it’s about helping children grow into well-rounded individuals. That’s why we offer a wide range of enriching activities, from visits to museums and theatres to sports clubs and music events. Our pupils are encouraged to develop a love of reading, take care of their physical and mental well-being, and develop the skills they need to succeed in the future.
Our work doesn’t stop at the classroom door. We focus on nurturing every child’s potential, including those with special educational needs and disabilities, and those who are learning English as an additional language. We take pride in ensuring that every pupil has the support they need to achieve their best, and we are grateful for the strong partnership we have with our parents and carers in this important work.
We are fully committed to safeguarding and ensuring the well-being of all our pupils. We have strong systems in place to keep our children safe, and our staff are well-trained to respond to any concerns swiftly and appropriately.
At William Davies, we know that every child is unique and has the ability to achieve great things. Together, we work hard to ensure that every pupil is supported, challenged, and inspired in their learning. Please explore our website to learn more about the many opportunities and experiences that make our school such a special place for children to grow and learn.
We look forward to welcoming you to our school community.
Sally Norris Headteacher
Statements of Practice
WDPS Inclusive Culture Statement
We are committed to cultivating an inclusive culture that ensures every individual feels seen, heard, represented and valued. By embracing diversity and promoting equity, we empower our children with the confidence, knowledge, and skills needed to succeed, and to support others to succeed. Through this approach, we aim to prepare them to lead with empathy and thrive in a global society.
WDPS Sustainability Statement
William Davies Primary School is committed to being a sustainable school. We believe that every child should understand their roles and responsibilities in looking after their environment, and should be given the opportunity to practise learning about, and leading, environmentally responsible lifestyles. We aim to raise awareness of our ecological footprint through both child-led projects and SLT initiatives, with the aim to reduce our carbon footprint a priority for all. We empower our children to be global citizens by giving them the skills and confidence to enact meaningful change in their local environments, and beyond. We are proud of our links to agencies who support us in achieving our sustainability goals: Keep Britain Tidy, WaterAid, Green Schools Project, Eco Schools, SusTrans and the British Council.
WDPS Digital Literacy Statement
We prioritise digital literacy to ensure the children are ready to live, learn, participate and thrive in a digital society. We equip children with essential skills for navigating the digital world, fostering critical thinking, creativity, including safe and ethical online behaviour.
At William Davies Primary School, we believe in fostering an inclusive environment in which all children can flourish; as a school community, we learn to understand and respect one another’s differences and needs. We provide all children with an understanding and experience of inclusion which they can carry into the next stage of their education and their future.

pageCache.pageTitle: PTA (Parent Teacher Association) – William Davies Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our school PTA aims to bring together parents, teachers and our local community to raise funds and to support our school.
Y1 & Reception’s Movie Night
The Association shall be known as the William Davies Primary School Parent Teacher Association (often simply referred to as the PTA).
The aims of the Association are to enrich the education and school experiences of the pupils of the school by bringing together the wider school community, running fundraising events and working with school staff.
The Members of the Association shall comprise all parents or guardians of children attending the school (including nursery class) and staff employed at the school. PTA committee members will be appointed annually.
The PTA committee shall consist of:
There will also be a minute taker at all PTA meetings.
Where a member of the Committee fails to attend regular meetings and does not play an active role in any of the activities of the Association, the committee reserves the right to ask the member to step down.
Meetings of the General Committee shall be held as required during term time. At all meetings of the Committee a third of General Committee Members, at least two, shall form a quorum. The committee will aim to meet once a month and more frequently if required for arrangements of events.
Each member of the committee shall have one vote and resolutions shall be passed by a simple majority vote of those present. The Chairman shall have the deciding vote which shall be used only in the event of a tie.
The Annual General Meeting (AGM) shall be held in June each year. The AGM will be advertised in the school newsletter and this is the responsibility of the secretary to organize.
The business shall include:-
At all Annual General Meetings voting shall be on the basis of one vote per member present at the meeting.
At all Annual General Meetings the quorum shall consist of no less than 2 members of the Association.
Any member of the Association shall have the right to raise a motion to be voted on at the Annual General Meeting by sending the motion in writing to the Secretary by no later than 10 days prior to the AGM.
Funds of the Association shall be lodged in a bank, building society or other account in the name of the Association. Cheques shall be drawn or withdrawals made against the signatures of two named Committee members.
The Treasurer shall be responsible for keeping accurate records of the financial transactions of the Association.
The Association’s financial year shall end on the last day of February in each year. The accounts shall be reviewed annually by an independent examiner appointed at the previous AGM by the members.
The Committee shall be responsible for ensuring that all property/money received by/for the Association shall be used in accordance with the aims of the Association.
Changes or additions must be made at an AGM or an EGM called for the purpose. The proposed change shall be specified in the notice calling the meeting and be approved by not less than two thirds of those present.
If it becomes necessary to dissolve the Association, by reason of it being impossible to achieve the objectives for which the Association is set up, this decision must be made by no less than 4 members of the Association voting in person and one of these members must be the chair person.
